customFields.title: Custom Fields
customFields.description: Manage your custom fields and configurations

error.unauthorized: Please log in as an administrator

organizations.title: $t(terms.organization)
organizations.description: Balance, revenue, profit, listings and ad spend of every participating $t(terms.organization). Click a column heading to sort.
organizations.supplyMismatch: * The MP ledger does not add up

tradeAnalysis.title: Trading bias
tradeAnalysis.lead: Shows mutual buying and reliance on a single partner as numbers.
tradeAnalysis.notice: This is not a judgement of cheating.
tradeAnalysis.detail: Buying from a friend because the product is genuinely good and buying from each other to score points look the same in the data. If a pair looks odd, ask the $t(terms.participant) themselves.

mutual.title: Mutual trade rate
mutual.description: Trade between the two $t(terms.organization) / total trade of those two $t(terms.organization). Pairs above {{threshold}}% are highlighted. Two $t(terms.organization) that trade only with each other reach 50% (the same amount is counted twice in the total).

concentration.title: Purchase concentration
concentration.lead: Share of everything a $t(terms.organization) bought that went to its biggest supplier.
concentration.notice: A $t(terms.organization) that bought from only one supplier is always at 100%.
concentration.detail: $t(terms.organization) that simply bought very few times also rise to the top, so read the number of suppliers and the amount together.

purchaseLog.title: $t(terms.administrator) purchase log
purchaseLog.lead: What each $t(terms.administrator) bought and for how much is
purchaseLog.detail: It is here so that a $t(terms.administrator) can notice their own unintended bias. $t(terms.participant) cannot see this page.

bySeller.title: By $t(terms.organization) (bought by $t(terms.administrator))
bySeller.description: The number of $t(terms.administrator) is shown as well, so you can tell whether one $t(terms.administrator) bought a lot or many $t(terms.administrator) bought a little.
